English: Grassland Pen
A makeshift livestock pen of woven brush and earthworks, hastily assembled by the first settlers to corral their herds on the open plains.
Open Range
Vast stretches of grassland marked only by simple boundary stones and watchfires, allowing herds to graze freely under clan supervision.
Plains Corral
A sturdy corral of timber and sod, providing better control over livestock during seasonal migrations across the grasslands.
Wooden Stockade
A fortified enclosure of sharpened logs, offering protection against predators and raiders, while increasing the security of valuable herds.
Roving Herd Field
Expansive fields mapped and rotated to prevent overgrazing, with roving herders and shelters to support year-round livestock movement.
Fenced Pasture
Broad, permanent pastures surrounded by sturdy fencing, supporting the expansion of large herds and the growth of nomadic prosperity.
Shepherds Hut
A network of huts for herders and their families, providing shelter, oversight, and improved coordination among the clans' stockmen.
Grazing Commons
Communal grazing lands administered by the elders, with shared resources and oversight fostering unity and efficient livestock management.
Plains Livestock Pavilion
A vast pavilion of felt and timber, serving as a seasonal center for fairs, livestock trade, and the gathering of nomadic chieftains.
Grand Plains Grazing Hall
A monumental hall of the plains, symbolizing the might of the plains clans, hosting livestock auctions, clan councils, and feasts of unity.
